notes.ios:
RefineID is a smart-card driver. It makes the certificates on a Finnish identity card (FINEID) available to the operating system, so Safari can use them to sign in to Finnish public e-services at suomi.fi, the government's national service portal. It also signs PDF documents with the card's qualified signature certificate.

There is no account to demonstrate. The app has no login, no RefineID cloud service, no registration, and collects no data. Nothing in it sits behind credentials, so there is no user name and password we can supply: none exists.

What the app needs is the card itself. The identity card is a legal identity document issued by the Finnish Police to one named citizen, in the same category as a passport; the certificates on it are issued by the Finnish Digital and Population Data Services Agency. It cannot be duplicated, transferred, or issued for testing, so we are unable to put one in the reviewer's hands.

VIRTUAL ID CARD - DEMONSTRATION MODE

In place of a card, this build carries a Virtual ID Card: an explicit, fictional identity card whose state a reviewer can inspect and edit. Every number on it is fictional and public in the source.

1. Press and hold the RefineID icon on the Home Screen and choose "Demo Mode". "DEMO MODE" is shown at the bottom of the screen for as long as the mode is on, and a red floating "Virtual ID Card" button stays on screen.
2. The app starts with a factory-fresh fictional card. Its numbers: card access number 123456, activation PIN 1234567. Walk the ordinary setup with them - enter the card access number and read the card. The card needs activation, so the Activate Card form opens: enter the activation PIN and choose a new PIN 1 (4 to 12 digits, for example 1234) and a new PIN 2 (6 to 12 digits, for example 123456). The screen then names the fictional holder, DOE JANE 12345678N. Pairing this iPhone with an iPad is done through the explicit in-app RAPP pairing; every remote operation needs holder approval on this phone, and CAN, PIN 1 and PIN 2 never leave it.
3. Tap the red Virtual ID Card button to open the card editor. It selects named card states - factory fresh, partially activated, activated, registered, and recovery states with low or blocked counters - and edits every value the UI reacts to: transport (NFC or reader), card presence, PIN 1, PIN 2 and PUK values and retry counters, certificate states, a pending signing request that supplies a fictional PDF, and one deterministic injected fault such as a lost connection or a card removed mid-operation. The activated states carry PIN 1 1234, PIN 2 123456 and PUK 12345678.
4. The ordinary product screens handle whatever is configured: PIN 1 and PIN 2 change, PIN reset with the PUK 12345678, the refusal that protects a card on its last two attempts, and qualified signing of the supplied fictional PDF with PIN 2 (the one chosen at activation, or 123456 on the activated states).

Demo Mode lasts one launch: only the Home Screen action turns it on, so no ordinary launch can enter it, and quitting the app ends it. Nothing in it touches a card or the system. No certificate is read, nothing is stored, no token is registered, and no output can be mistaken for a genuine card signature: the fictional holder has no certificate, so the system is offered no identity.

Also verifiable without a card:
- Every screen is available in English, Finnish and Swedish, and with VoiceOver, larger text, and the dark interface. The fictional holder is named in each language.

With a real card, this build reads the card over the iPhone's NFC antenna or a connected USB-C smart-card reader, publishes the card's certificates to the system for Safari, and signs PDF documents with PIN 2.

The complete source is public at https://github.com/refineid/refineid-apple, including the card protocol and the whole Virtual ID Card harness, so the behaviour behind the card can be read directly.
notes.macos:
RefineID is a smart-card driver. It makes the certificates on a Finnish identity card (FINEID) available to the operating system, so Safari can use them to sign in to Finnish public e-services at suomi.fi, the national e-service portal. It also signs PDF documents with the card's qualified signature certificate.

There is no account to demonstrate: no login, no RefineID cloud service, no registration, no data collection. Nothing sits behind credentials, so there is no user name and password to supply.

What the app needs is the card itself. The identity card is a legal identity document issued by the Finnish Police to one named citizen, like a passport; its certificates come from the Finnish Digital and Population Data Services Agency. It cannot be duplicated, transferred, or issued for testing, so we cannot put one in the reviewer's hands.

VIRTUAL ID CARD - DEMONSTRATION MODE

In place of a card and reader, this build carries a Virtual ID Card: a fictional identity card in a fictional reader whose state a reviewer can inspect and edit. Every number on it is fictional and public in the source.

1. Choose View > Demo Mode (Option-Command-D). "DEMO MODE" is shown in red across the foot of the window while the mode is on, and a red "Virtual ID Card" button floats in the lower right corner.
2. Demo Mode starts with a factory-fresh fictional card, so the Activate Card form is shown. Enter the activation PIN 1234567 and choose a new PIN 1 (4 to 12 digits, for example 1234) and a new PIN 2 (6 to 12 digits, for example 123456). The window then names the fictional holder, DOE JANE 12345678N, and offers document signing.
3. Click the Virtual ID Card button, or choose View > Edit Virtual Card... (Option-Command-E), to open the editor. It selects named card states - factory fresh, activated, recovery with low or blocked counters - and edits every value the UI reacts to: card presence, PIN and PUK values with retry counters, certificate states, a pending signing request that supplies a fictional PDF, and one injected fault such as a card removed mid-operation. Return applies, Escape cancels. Activated states carry PIN 1 1234, PIN 2 123456 and PUK 12345678.
4. The ordinary screens handle whatever is configured: PIN changes, PIN reset with the PUK 12345678, the retry floor refusal that protects a card on its last two attempts, and qualified signing of a PDF with PIN 2 (chosen at activation, or 123456 on an activated card). Drop any PDF onto the window, or turn on "Signing request pending" and a fictional PDF is supplied.
5. Choosing View > Demo Mode again turns it off, and quitting ends it: the state lives only in the running process. Nothing in it touches a card or the system - no certificate is read, nothing is stored in the keychain, no token is registered - and no output can be mistaken for a genuine card signature.

NETWORK AND APP TRANSPORT SECURITY

- The app connects out only while signing an archival document: the fixed qualified time-stamp authority http://timestamp.sectigo.com/qualified (RFC 3161), revocation endpoints (OCSP, RFC 6960; CRL, RFC 5280) read from the certificate being validated, and the EU trusted lists that anchor its time stamp.
- App Transport Security is therefore open: NSAllowsArbitraryLoads, with the fixed authority also named in NSExceptionDomains. Revocation and trusted-list hosts arrive at runtime from certificates and from the EU List of the Lists, so an exception-domain list cannot enumerate them, and qualified providers may answer over HTTP. The signing client enforces the rest: public IPs only, http and https only, response caps, re-vetted redirects, and verification of every certificate and token.
- This Mac build has no remote card: no Bluetooth, no local network, no incoming connections, no local server. The Virtual ID Card above is the review path.

The complete source is public at https://github.com/refineid/refineid-apple, including the card protocol.

Identity card reader and signing tool.

You can also use your phone wirelessly as a card reader.

whatToTest.ios:
• Set up a card over NFC: check that the app keeps the CAN and retries after a missed scan. Check that an incorrect CAN returns to entry and Cancel stops scanning.
• Check the shorter QR reader title in English, Finnish and Swedish.
• Sign and verify documents, and use the card from a paired iPad.
whatToTest.macos:
Mac App Store candidate for 26.11.20.
• Connect a USB smart card reader, insert your identity card, then activate the card and manage PIN codes.
• Sign a PDF or ASiC document, and sign in to e-services in Safari with the card. Signing now completes on a first run with an empty trusted-list cache.
• Remote use through a phone is not part of this release.
